findings.title: Black Money Act 2015 exposure on undisclosed foreign assets — up to $312,000 at stake
findings.detail: $260,000 of foreign asset value is undisclosed on Schedule FA (same forms-disagree fact as above). The Black Money Act imposes a flat 30% tax ($78,000) on the asset value PLUS a penalty of up to 3x that tax (up to $234,000) — up to $312,000 total (120% of the asset's value) — PLUS possible prosecution (up to 10 years' rigorous imprisonment for willful evasion), independent of and in addition to the monetary exposure.
findings.recommendation: Correct the Schedule FA disclosure before this compounds further. FAST-DS 2026 (a one-time amnesty window, gap tracker XB-21) offers a much cheaper cure — 30% tax + 30% penalty (60% total) if the asset/income was never taxed, or a flat ₹1,00,000 fee if it was bought from already-taxed income or acquired while genuinely NRI.

findings.title: Foreign Tax Credit shortfall — residual double taxation
findings.detail: Indian tax paid ($9,524) exceeds the US FTC limitation ($8,456) for this year. $1,068 of Indian tax cannot be credited currently and would otherwise be double-taxed.
findings.recommendation: $1,068 is eligible to carry over under §904(c) (back 1 year / forward 10), but WISING is a single-year snapshot — it does NOT persist this carryover across tax years or track it for you. Record $1,068 on Form 1116 Schedule B this year, and re-enter it as prior-year carryover when you run next year's numbers. Also check whether treaty re-sourcing (Art. 25) could reclassify some income to lift the limitation — WISING does not test this automatically.

findings.title: PFIC exposure: Indian mutual funds
findings.detail: 2 Indian mutual fund / ETF holding(s) detected. For a US person these are Passive Foreign Investment Companies — taxed under the punitive §1291 excess-distribution regime by default, with a separate Form 8621 per fund.
findings.recommendation: Evaluate a QEF or Mark-to-Market election (must be timely). Many Indian AMCs cannot supply a PFIC Annual Information Statement, which can force the §1291 default — consider restructuring holdings to US-domiciled funds.

findings.title: Layer 1 forms disagree: India form says 'no foreign assets', US form shows foreign holdings
findings.detail: The India intake form explicitly records NO foreign assets, but the US intake form shows US-source income and/or non-Indian accounts for the same taxpayer — who is an Indian ROR this year and therefore subject to worldwide Schedule FA disclosure. This is a direct contradiction between the two forms, not just a missing field.
findings.recommendation: Reconcile the two forms before filing: either the India form's 'no foreign assets' answer needs correcting, or the US-side accounts/income need to be re-checked. Schedule FA penalties for non-disclosure are severe and independent of whether any tax is actually due on the asset.

findings.title: FBAR threshold breached
findings.detail: Aggregate peak balance across foreign accounts is $56,626, above the USD 10,000 reporting cliff. EVERY foreign account must be reported, not just those over the limit.
findings.recommendation: File FinCEN Form 114 by the due date (auto-extended to Oct 15). Non-willful penalties start at ~$10,000 per violation; willful penalties are far higher.

findings.title: US Alternative Minimum Tax applies (+$32,345)
findings.detail: This is a US-only tax (IRC §55) — India has no AMT-equivalent regime. The US tentative minimum tax exceeds the regular US tax, so an additional $32,345 is added to the US liability. Common drivers: a large standard-deduction / SALT add-back, private-activity-bond interest, or an ISO exercise.
findings.recommendation: WISING computes the parallel AMT (Form 6251) and includes it in the US tax total above. Review ISO exercise timing and the state-tax add-back; AMT paid on deferral items can generate a Minimum Tax Credit (Form 8801) usable in later years.

findings.title: California state income tax: $15,383 (Form 540)
findings.detail: California taxes a full-year resident's WORLDWIDE income, including Indian-source income already reported on the federal and Indian returns — computed here as $245,301 of state taxable income (federal AGI $256,713 less the California standard deduction) at California's own bracket rates, less $307 of personal/dependent credits. Neither the Foreign Tax Credit computed above nor any DTAA relief applies here — California is not a party to the India-US treaty and grants no credit for tax paid to a foreign country at all.
findings.recommendation: File Form 540 alongside the federal return. This is a full-year-resident, TY2025-rates estimate — it does not split state-source income for a part-year or nonresident allocation, does not model California's own AGI addition/subtraction adjustments beyond the standard deduction, and (for California) does not include the local-jurisdiction SDI/VPDI payroll tax. Treat as directional, not filing-ready.

findings.title: US estimated-tax underpayment penalty — Form 2210 ($1,093 estimated)
findings.detail: Withholding + estimated payments ($31,000) fall short of both safe harbors: 90% of this year's tax ($55,519) and the prior-year safe harbor (last year's total tax was never entered, so only the current-year harbor could be checked), with a balance due over the $1,000 de-minimis. Estimated penalty (simplified regular method, equal quarterly installments, withholding spread evenly, no cross-quarter netting): $1,093.
findings.recommendation: Confirm against the real Form 2210 (it can use the Annualized Income Installment Method for uneven income, which this estimate does not model, and could produce a lower number). Paying the shortfall now stops further accrual.

findings.title: AMZN foreign equity holding: 18 months held — India says STCG, US says LTCG ($1,040 at stake)
findings.detail: This unlisted foreign equity holding was held 18 months. India requires more than 24 months for LTCG on unlisted shares, so this is STCG there (taxed at your India slab rate). The US requires only more than 12 months for LTCG on any asset — no listed/unlisted distinction — so the SAME gain is LTCG under US rules. Recomputed your actual US return both ways: treated as LTCG, US tax is $71,647; treated as STCG (ordinary rates), US tax is $72,687 — a difference of $1,040.
findings.recommendation: Report this gain as LONG-TERM on the US return (Schedule D) even though it's short-term in India — using India's label on the US foreign-capital-gains input would cost roughly $1,040 in overpaid US tax.

findings.title: Indian retirement accounts (EPF / PPF / NPS) are taxed differently by the US
findings.detail: India treats EPF, PPF and NPS as tax-free (or lightly taxed). The US does not automatically agree: the IRS can tax the interest these accounts earn every year, and may treat PPF like a trust that needs extra forms. Layer 1 already records $542 of EPF interest as taxable this year — WISING has added that amount to the US taxable income and tax figures shown elsewhere on this page (as ordinary foreign-source interest/pension), so it isn't just displayed here without effect.
findings.recommendation: WISING does NOT determine whether a specific account is a treaty-protected pension under DTAA Art. 20, or whether PPF should be treated as a foreign trust requiring Form 3520/3520-A — those are legal/factual determinations you need to make yourself; Form 3520 only appears on the filing checklist when the separate PPF/EPF-plus-US-residency trigger fires, not because this specific check ran. Confirm the treaty-protection question and trust classification before relying on the totals above.

findings.title: NIIT / Additional Medicare surtaxes are not offset by the Foreign Tax Credit
findings.detail: NIIT $255 (§1411, 3.8%) applies on top of regular US income tax. Indian income tax can only credit the REGULAR US income tax (§901/§904) — these two surtaxes are outside the FTC mechanism entirely, so they stand as double taxation even when the rest of the Indian tax is fully credited.
findings.recommendation: There is no credit path for this residue — the only levers are reducing MAGI/net investment income (retirement contributions, timing) or, for Additional Medicare, W-4 withholding planning. Make sure the client understands the FTC reconciliation above does not clear this amount.

findings.title: India residency status may not match the facts on file — derived RNOR, recorded ROR
findings.detail: Re-deriving India's residential-status determination from the same raw facts Layer 1's own wizard uses (day-count, the 4-year lookback, RNOR sub-status conditions, employment/PIO-visit exceptions, s.6(1A) deemed-residency, incorporation/POEM, or control-and-management, depending on entity type) produces RNOR, but the recorded final_india_residency_status is ROR.
findings.recommendation: Re-run the Layer 1 India residency wizard, or verify the underlying residency facts were entered consistently — this looks like a wizard or data-entry error.

findings.title: State tax residency is not resolved by the DTAA / federal treaty position (CA)
findings.detail: The India-US treaty and the federal residency determination above bind FEDERAL tax only. CA applies its own domicile or statutory-day residency test, independent of the Article 4 tie-breaker or any §911/1040NR position. A taxpayer can be a federal treaty non-resident while remaining a full worldwide-income STATE resident with Indian income fully taxable and no matching relief in some states.
findings.recommendation: Run the state's own residency test (domicile intent + day count) separately from the federal/treaty analysis. California safe-harbor/retained-ties facts are on file — CA is aggressive about domicile and does not allow a credit for foreign tax paid. Do not assume the federal treaty position carries over.

findings.title: LRS remittance approaching limit
findings.detail: Outbound LRS remittances of $204,819 are at 82% of the USD 250,000 RBI annual cap.
findings.recommendation: Monitor remaining headroom for the rest of the financial year; TCS at 20% applies above ₹10 lakh.

findings.title: Equity compensation taxed on both sides — cross-border sourcing not applied
findings.detail: Both an India ESOP/perquisite event and a US equity-compensation event (RSU vest / NSO exercise) are on file for this year. India taxes the ESOP perquisite in full at exercise/allotment (s.17(1)(vi)); the US taxes RSU vesting / NSO exercise in full as ordinary income in the vesting/exercise year. Absent a workday-based allocation, the same equity award can be fully taxed by BOTH countries rather than apportioned to where the services were actually performed during the vesting period.
findings.recommendation: Reconstruct the vesting-period workday split between India and the US (DTAA Art. 15/16 dependent-personal-services sourcing) so each country only taxes its proportionate share, then claim FTC/§159 relief on the genuinely overlapping portion rather than the full award twice.

findings.title: 6 income head(s) taxed under both codes — see reconciliation
findings.detail: The same income is taxed in India (its own Act) and the US (the IRC): Salary / Wages, Business / Professional, House property / Rental, Interest, Dividend, Capital gains. Overlapping exposure of $39,747 is what the FTC / §159 relief resolves. Some heads are planning-grade estimates pending line-item inputs.
findings.recommendation: Open the Cross-Basis Reconciliation on the Filings tab to see each head on both bases, then relieve the overlap via Form 1116 (US) / Form 44 (India).

findings.title: Dual residency resolved under DTAA Article 4 → US
findings.detail: Both India and the US met residency, and the Layer 1 Article 4 tie-breaker resolves treaty residence to US for the overlapping period (Art. 4(2)(a): centre of vital interests is closer to the US). WISING has applied this to the tax and FTC computation below; the loser jurisdiction is taxed on a source basis.
findings.recommendation: Keep Form 8833 (US) and TRC + Form 41 (India) on file to support the position.

findings.title: ISO exercise(s) on file — employer owes you Form 3921
findings.detail: 1 incentive stock option exercise(s) recorded this year. The employer is required to furnish Form 3921 (one per exercise) by January 31 of the following year, reporting the grant/exercise dates, exercise price, and FMV at exercise — the same figures already driving the AMT preference computed above.
findings.recommendation: Confirm Form 3921 was received from the employer for each exercise and that its FMV/exercise-price figures match what's on file here before relying on the AMT number.

findings.title: Brought-forward losses fully set off this year
findings.detail: All eligible prior-year losses were absorbed against this year's income: ₹1,80,000 STCG loss vs. slab-rate STCG (s.69 unlisted buy-back). The India tax computed above already reflects this — no residual carry-forward remains.
findings.recommendation: Confirm the set-off is reported correctly on Schedule CFL/BFLA of the ITR, matching the ordering above.

findings.title: Form 44 — required for the Indian FTC claim
findings.detail: Foreign income / foreign tax is present, so India requires Form 44 (with Schedule FSI and TR) on or before the ITR due date to allow FTC u/s 90/91.
findings.recommendation: WISING flags Form 44 (with Schedule FSI/TR) as required on the filing checklist, using the FSI/TR figures already computed above — actually preparing and e-filing it on the income-tax portal ahead of the ITR due date is still a manual step.

findings.title: Tax-year apportionment: Indian FY ↔ US CY (computed)
findings.detail: India taxes Apr–Mar; the US taxes Jan–Dec. WISING splits the Indian FY across US calendar years — $37,925 into CY2026 and $12,642 into CY2027 (Indian quarterly data) — and apportions the US calendar year into the Indian FY (9/12 + 3/12).
findings.recommendation: See the FY ↔ CY Apportionment panel on the Filings tab for the period-matched figures behind Form 44 (India) and Form 1116 (US). Planning-grade — refine with per-transaction dates at filing.

findings.title: FX conversion basis is an approximation
findings.detail: Cross-border amounts are normalized at a flat 83 INR/USD. Statutory FTC computations require the telegraphic-transfer buying rate on the relevant date (Rule 115 / SBI TTBR).
findings.recommendation: Re-price each foreign income and tax item at the correct per-transaction rate before filing; the flat rate is for planning visibility only.

findings.title: Indian company held below the 10% CFC threshold
findings.detail: 1 Indian business interest(s) on file, but Layer 1 shows US ownership below 10% — so Form 5471 Category 5 / GILTI do not apply this year.
findings.recommendation: No 5471 action needed at current ownership. WISING recomputes this every time you re-run the numbers, so update the ownership percentage in Layer 1 as soon as a purchase or reorganization changes it — this isn't monitored in the background.

documents.name: FinCEN Form 114 (FBAR)
documents.desc: Report of Foreign Bank and Financial Accounts.

documents.name: IRS Form 8938 (FATCA)

documents.name: IRS Form 1116 (Foreign Tax Credit)
documents.desc: Claims credit for income tax paid to India against US tax liability.
documents.why: Indian income tax was paid on income that is also taxable in the US.

documents.name: IRS Form 2555 (FEIE)

documents.why: FEIE was elected on foreign earned income.

documents.name: IRS Form 8833 (Treaty-Based Position)

documents.why: A DTAA tie-breaker or treaty rate is being relied upon to override default US taxation.

documents.name: IRS Form 8621 (PFIC)
documents.desc: Information return for Passive Foreign Investment Companies — one per fund.
documents.why: Holdings in Indian mutual funds / ETFs are PFICs and require annual reporting (punitive §1291 regime unless QEF/MTM elected).

documents.name: IRS Form 5471 (CFC)
documents.desc: Information return for US persons owning ≥10% of a foreign corporation.
documents.why: You own ≥10% of an Indian company — potential Subpart F / GILTI inclusion.

documents.name: IRS Form 8865
documents.desc: Return for US persons with interests in a foreign partnership.
documents.why: You hold an interest in an Indian partnership/LLP.

documents.name: IRS Form 3520 / 3520-A
documents.desc: Reporting of foreign gifts and transactions with foreign trusts.
documents.why: Foreign gift > USD 100,000 received, or you are a grantor/beneficiary of a foreign trust (note: Indian PPF/EPF may be treated as trusts).

documents.name: IRS Form 1040-NR
documents.desc: Non-resident alien income tax return.
documents.why: You are (or elect to be treated as) a US non-resident alien for this year.

documents.name: IRS Form 8960 (NIIT)
documents.desc: Net Investment Income Tax (3.8%).
documents.why: MAGI exceeded the NIIT threshold and net investment income is present.

documents.name: IRS Form 8959 (Additional Medicare Tax)
documents.desc: Additional 0.9% Medicare tax on wages/SE income above the filing-status threshold, and reconciles employer over/under-withholding.
documents.why: Additional Medicare Tax is owed and is not offset by the Foreign Tax Credit.

documents.name: California Form 540 (Resident Income Tax Return)
documents.desc: California state income tax return — computed on worldwide income for a full-year CA resident, including Indian-source income. CA grants no credit for tax paid to a foreign country.
documents.why: State-of-residence facts on file point to California, and CA taxes worldwide income independently of the federal treaty position.

documents.name: New York Form IT-201 (Resident Income Tax Return)
documents.desc: New York state income tax return — computed on worldwide income for a full-year NY resident, including Indian-source income. NY grants no credit for tax paid to a foreign country.
documents.why: State-of-residence facts on file point to New York, and NY taxes worldwide income independently of the federal treaty position.

documents.name: Form 44 (India FTC)
documents.desc: Statement of foreign income & foreign tax, filed before the ITR due date.
documents.why: Foreign (US) income is being offered to tax in India and FTC u/s 90/91 is claimed. Schedule FSI/TR must accompany the ITR.

documents.name: Tax Residency Certificate (TRC)
documents.desc: Issued by the other contracting state (IRS Form 6166 for the US).
documents.why: DTAA relief / treaty rate is being claimed — a TRC is mandatory u/s 159(8).

documents.name: Form 41
documents.desc: Self-declaration accompanying the TRC, filed electronically on the ITR portal.
documents.why: Treaty benefit claimed and the TRC does not contain all particulars required u/r 75.

documents.name: Schedule FA (Foreign Assets)
documents.desc: Disclosure of foreign assets/accounts in the Indian ITR.
documents.why: You are Resident & Ordinarily Resident (ROR) and hold US bank accounts, securities or other foreign assets.

documents.name: Schedule FSI & Schedule TR
documents.desc: Foreign Source Income and Tax Relief schedules in the ITR.
documents.why: Foreign income is offered to tax and relief u/s 90/91 is claimed.

documents.name: Form 145 / Form 146 (was 15CA / 15CB)
documents.desc: Remittance certificates for foreign outward remittances.
documents.why: Outward remittances under LRS / to non-residents were made during the year. Renumbered from Form 15CA/15CB effective 1 Apr 2026 under the Income-tax Rules, 2026 (Rule 220) — the old numbers still apply to remittances made before that date.

documents.name: Schedule AL (Assets & Liabilities)
documents.desc: Disclosure of assets and liabilities at cost, filed with the ITR.
documents.why: Total income exceeds ₹50 lakh — Schedule AL is mandatory at this threshold u/s 139(1) (ITR-2/3/5 filers).

documents.name: Form 3CB / 3CD (Tax Audit Report)
documents.desc: Chartered Accountant's tax-audit report and statement of particulars, filed before the ITR due date.
documents.why: Business turnover exceeds the s.44AB tax-audit threshold (₹1 crore, or ₹10 crore where cash receipts and payments are each ≤5% of the total).

documents.name: IRS Form 8802 (Application for US Residency Certification)
documents.desc: Application to the IRS for Form 6166 — the US residency certificate India's TRC requirement expects the other contracting state to issue.
documents.why: DTAA relief is being claimed on Indian-source income — Form 6166 must be requested via Form 8802 before it can be filed with the Indian TRC/Form 41 paperwork; IRS processing typically takes 4-6+ weeks, so file well ahead of the India due date.

documents.name: IRS Form 6251 (Alternative Minimum Tax)
documents.desc: Computes AMT and reconciles it against regular tax liability.
documents.why: AMT preference items (commonly an ISO exercise, or the SALT-cap add-back) push tentative minimum tax above the regular tax for the year.

documents.name: IRS Form 8288 / 8288-A / 8288-B (FIRPTA Withholding)
documents.desc: Withholding certificate and returns for a foreign person's disposition of US real property.
documents.why: A US real property interest was disposed of by a foreign person — 15% FIRPTA withholding applies at closing unless a Form 8288-B withholding certificate reduces it.

documents.name: Form 3CEB (Transfer Pricing Certification)
documents.desc: Chartered Accountant's report on international transactions with associated enterprises, filed before the ITR due date u/s 92E.
documents.why: A cross-border related-party ownership relationship is on file — international transactions with that entity must be reported and certified, independent of whether pricing is at arm's length.

documents.name: Form 26AS / AIS / TIS
documents.desc: Annual tax-credit statement (26AS) and the Annual/Taxpayer Information Statements — the pre-filled record every ITR should be reconciled against before filing.
documents.why: Indian income is on file for this taxpayer — TDS, advance tax and reported high-value transactions should be cross-checked against these statements before the return is filed.

documents.name: Form 16 / Form 16A (TDS Certificates)
documents.desc: Salary (Form 16) and non-salary (Form 16A) TDS certificates issued by each deductor.
documents.why: Indian income subject to TDS is on file — hold the certificate from each deductor to reconcile against Form 26AS/AIS and support the credit claimed in the ITR.

documents.name: LRS Form A2 (Outward Remittance Declaration)
documents.desc: Declaration furnished to the remitting bank for each outward remittance under the Liberalised Remittance Scheme.
documents.why: Outward remittances under LRS were made this year — each remittance requires its own Form A2 filed with the bank at the time of transfer, separate from the annual Form 145/146 (was 15CA/15CB) return-time reporting.

documents.name: IRS Form 4868 (Extension Request)
documents.desc: Automatic 6-month extension of time to file (not to pay) the US return.
documents.why: Must be filed by the original due date to legally reach the extended deadline already on your Compliance Calendar — the extension does not happen automatically.

scopeNotes.title: GAAR is not evaluated
scopeNotes.body: India's General Anti-Avoidance Rule can recharacterize arrangements that lack commercial substance — a facts-and-circumstances judgment no rules engine can safely make. WISING flags mechanical conflicts only; whether an arrangement invites GAAR scrutiny remains a professional call.

scopeNotes.title: STT is not computed as a levy
scopeNotes.body: Securities Transaction Tax charged on trades (raised on F&O by Finance Act 2026) isn't calculated here. The stt_paid flag on each transaction drives the capital-gains regime (s.196/198 vs s.197) — the levy amount itself is neither a tax credit nor a capital-gains deduction, so nothing downstream depends on it.

scopeNotes.title: Your obligations as a TDS deductor aren't tracked
scopeNotes.body: The Withholding page covers tax withheld FROM this taxpayer's income. Duties in the opposite direction — deducting TDS on payments the business makes to vendors, contractors, or professionals — aren't monitored as a compliance obligation in their own right, though the resulting s.40(a) expense disallowance for TDS failures (and s.40A(3) cash-payment / s.43B(h) MSME-overdue disallowances) does flow into business income (Phase 1).

scopeNotes.title: Clubbing amounts are taken as entered
scopeNotes.body: Spousal and minor-child clubbed income entered in Layer 1 is taxed as given. WISING doesn't trace asset transfers between family members to detect clubbing that should have been reported but wasn't.

scopeNotes.title: FICA/FUTA levies aren't computed
scopeNotes.body: Employee and employer Social Security/Medicare/unemployment payroll taxes are a separate tax base from income tax. Only the pieces that touch the 1040 are computed: Additional Medicare 0.9%, self-employment tax, and the W-2 withholding shown on the Withholding page.

scopeNotes.title: FATCA Chapter 4 withholding is institution-side
scopeNotes.body: The 30% FATCA withholding regime (IRC §§1471-1474) applies to payments to non-compliant foreign financial institutions — banks' problem, not yours directly. Where it touches an individual is the US-person self-certification banks request, which is tracked with your documents.

scopeNotes.title: Document-upload extraction is simulated
scopeNotes.body: Every "upload to auto-fill" feature in Layer 1 (Form 26AS, Lower-TDS certificate, bank statements, property documents) is a demo simulation with representative values — not live OCR. Figures sourced from an upload should be treated as manually-entered until real extraction ships.

scopeNotes.title: MLI does not affect the India-US treaty
scopeNotes.body: The US never signed the OECD Multilateral Instrument, so the India-US DTAA text is untouched by it — unlike India's treaties with the UK, Netherlands, or Singapore. Verified; nothing to apply.

scopeNotes.title: Treaty text current as modeled
scopeNotes.body: The India-US DTAA has not been amended since the 2000 protocol. Every treaty rate and tie-breaker rule in this engine reflects the treaty as it stands.

Reasons: Capital gains beyond the s.198-only allowance (STCG and/or non-s.198 LTCG present); Brought-forward losses on file. Layer 1 India hasn't produced its own recommendation for this profile (itr_recommendation.form is unset) — this is WISING's own independent computation, run unconditionally, not a hedge pending the frontend.
